title: T2 Due Date for a January 31 Year-End
meta_description: A January 31 year-end makes the T2 due July 31. Filing is mandatory even with no activity. Nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus HST per tax year.
content:
A January 31 year-end makes the T2 due July 31, six months after the end of the tax year.

Every resident corporation, including an inactive one, must file a T2 return within six months of its fiscal year-end, every year, until it is formally dissolved. A final T2 is due within six months of dissolution. Having no revenue, no bank activity and no employees does not remove the obligation.

Due dates by tax year

Fiscal year-endT2 due
January 31, 2025July 31, 2025
January 31, 2026July 31, 2026
January 31, 2027July 31, 2027 (falls on a Saturday, so August 02, 2027)

Where a due date falls on a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday recognised by the Canada Revenue Agency, a return received the next business day is on time.

Filing a nil return for this year-end

This service is for a corporation with no activity in the tax year. A corporation with investment income, rental income, or dividends paid or received is not nil.

We are a registered EFILE electronic filer. Your return is transmitted to the Canada Revenue Agency electronically, and your CRA confirmation is emailed within 3 business days. Business days are Monday to Friday and exclude Ontario statutory holidays.

What it costs

$300.00 plus HST per tax year. One price for every year and every province. No hourly billing and no add-on fees.
